scope: Nomenclature and historical source reconciliation only; no photographs, new occurrence claims or current legal register.

primaryPdfs.access: Existing verified copy of the official book on a third-party mirror; previous complete transcription reused.
Existing consolidated copy of resolution 170/2005 as amended by 471/2009; comparison pages rendered again. Not a verified 2026 legal edition.

additionalSources.finding: Tulipa rosea Vved. is treated as a synonym of Tulipa korolkowii; agrees with the previous exact GBIF synonym and the already published taxon key 5299568.
Hedlundia persica accepted; Sorbus persica is a homotypic synonym. Kyrgyzstan is included in the distribution.
Prunus petunnikowii accepted; Amygdalus petunnikowii is a homotypic synonym. Kyrgyzstan is included.

additionalSources.accessMethod: web text of type record; image not downloaded
additionalSources.finding: Type of Kosopoljanskia hebecarpa catalogued under accepted Schrenkia hebecarpa; country Kyrgyzstan. Used only for identity, not photograph preparation.

additionalSources.publisher: Plant Diversity of Central Asia 1 (2022), 21–51; University of Helsinki repository
additionalSources.finding: Page 43 gives the homotypic combination Schrenkia turkestanica = Kosopoljanskia turkestanica and distribution including Talas, Kyrgyzstan.

additionalSources.publisher: Sennikov, Lazkov, Uotila & Weber, Taxonomic corrections and new records in vascular plants of Kyrgyzstan (2011)
additionalSources.finding: Documents Eriophyton anomalum as a new combination from Erianthera anomala, discusses the former Alajja concepts and Kyrgyz specimens. No extra taxon is created for the alternative genera.

Moluccella olgae accepted, with Otostegia schennikovii a heterotypic synonym. The accepted range includes Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan. A future card must restrict historical descriptions to the national named concept.

Salvia vvedenskii Nikitina accepted; original publication Flora Kirgizskoi SSR 10:377 (1962), range Kyrgyzstan. National Salvia vvedenskyi E. Nikit. is reconciled by the same author and a subsequent exact GBIF query, not by fuzzy matching alone.

Rhaponticum aulieatense accepted by POWO; Leuzea aulieatensis and Stemmacantha aulieatensis are homotypic alternatives. GBIF chooses Leuzea; the genus preference differs but the named species and rank are linked explicitly. The national account itself gives Rhaponticum as an alternative.
Richteria leontopodium accepted; Pyrethrum leontopodium a homotypic synonym; distribution includes Kyrgyzstan.

Dorema microcarpum is a homotypic synonym of Ferula namanganica in POWO, whereas the GBIF response chooses Ferula microcarpum. POWO lists Uzbekistan only. Preferred valid name, GBIF linkage and the national geographic concept need a combined review; retained in B.

additionalSources.publisher: American Society of Mammalogists; Mammal Diversity Database
additionalSources.finding: Rhinolophus hipposideros previously included R. midas; current authorship is André 1797 rather than the commonly cited Bechstein dates. Exact GBIF spelling alone cannot settle the national account's Iran–Turan subspecies concept.

additionalSources.publisher: American Society of Mammalogists; Mammal Diversity Database
additionalSources.finding: Rhinolophus midas is split from R. hipposideros, with Iran and Oman in its country list; cites Benda et al. 2023, DOI 10.3161/15081109ACC2022.24.2.001. No automatic transfer of Kyrgyz records to either species.

accessLimitations: A direct POWO API request returned a Cloudflare challenge; no attempt was made to bypass it. Primary taxon-page text available through web was used instead.

The catalog-125 cache was initially omitted from the query selection. Final reconciliation includes it: 15 repeated name matches are disclosed, 13 completed missing accepted-name records and two produced no new match information. Classification is unchanged; old caches are never overwritten.
The unamended 2005 list is not available in the verified materials; names behind 17 removed positions remain null. They are not reconstructed from guesses.

queryReuseAudit.note: Repeated match requests are disclosed rather than described as previously unresearched. No further duplicate queries performed.
